q: What does `g` hold after this runs?
why: `[row] * 2` repeats the same list object, so both rows change. Use `[[0] * 2 for _ in range(2)]`.

q: Rotating an n×n matrix 90° clockwise moves cell (r, c) to…
why: Row r becomes column n-1-r. Check on 3×3: the top-left (0,0) goes to the top-right (0,2).

q: Which pair of in-place steps rotates a square matrix clockwise?
options: Reverse each row, then reverse each column
Reverse the row order, then reverse each row
why: Transpose turns rows into columns; reversing each row then gives the clockwise turn.

q: Summing both diagonals of an n×n matrix directly takes…
why: Each row contributes two cells, (i, i) and (i, n-1-i): 2n reads.

q: Set Matrix Zeroes: why not zero a row and column the moment you find a 0?
options: The new zeros look like original ones and wipe out extra rows and columns
Python can't modify lists while looping
why: Record first, write second. Otherwise cells you zeroed trigger more zeroing later in the scan.
